milestones.label: Legal age to buy alcohol
milestones.population: retail purchasers of alcoholic beverages in the United States
whatChanges: Buying alcohol at retail becomes lawful at this threshold, which is the minimum legal drinking age in the United States.
Congress reached it through funding rather than a direct ban on sale: the federal statute withholds a share of a state's apportionment.
Stores, bars and restaurants ask for proof of age, so carrying identification becomes part of ordinary social occasions for many people.

milestones.label: Legal age to buy tobacco and nicotine products
milestones.population: retail purchasers of tobacco and nicotine products in the United States
whatChanges: Federal law raised the minimum age of sale for tobacco products to this threshold, so retail purchase becomes lawful for the buyer at this point.
The rule reaches the whole category, including cigarettes, cigars, smokeless tobacco and electronic nicotine products, rather than only combustible cigarettes.
Retailers check identification at the counter and at online checkout, so proof of age is part of these purchases.

milestones.label: Federal requirement for dependent coverage on a parent's plan ends
milestones.population: children covered as dependents under a group health plan or health insurance coverage that makes dependent coverage of children available
whatChanges: The federal floor runs out here: a plan that offers dependent coverage of children is no longer required by that rule to keep it available.
State rules and individual plans vary, and some carry dependent coverage past this point, so what actually happens turns on the particular plan and state.
Where coverage does end, it comes from somewhere else instead: an employer plan, a marketplace plan, a school plan, or a public program.

milestones.label: Automatic independent status for federal student aid
whatChanges: An applicant meets the statutory definition of an independent student on age alone, without having to satisfy any of the other conditions the law lists.
The law fixes the test to a set date within the award year rather than to the applicant's birthday, so the aid year matters as much as the age.
Younger applicants can still reach independent status through the other conditions in the same definition; age is one route among several.
